story_type: broken moon rover fender fixed with a map and tape, Apollo 17 mission film
hook: On the Moon, a broken fender was spraying them with dust.
narration: On the Moon, a broken fender was spraying them with dust.
December 1972. Gene Cernan and Jack Schmitt were driving their rover across the valley of Taurus Littrow.
Then they broke a rear fender, and the dust thrown up by the wheels began causing trouble.
Moon dust is fine and clings to everything. On equipment it soaks up sunlight and can make things overheat.
And time was short. There are only so many hours of oxygen and water in the backpacks.
That night on Earth, Apollo 16 commander John Young worked in a pressure suit on a way to fix it.
[short pause] On the Moon, they built a new fender from a folded lunar map and tape, held on with clamps from the lander.
outcome: The map and tape fender held for the rest of the mission.
title: Moon rover fixed with a map and tape
description:
In December 1972, Apollo 17 astronauts broke a rear fender on their lunar rover, and the dust it threw became a problem. Working from a fix tested on Earth by John Young, they built a new fender from a lunar map, tape and clamps, and it lasted the rest of the mission. From the NASA film Apollo 17: On the Shoulders of Giants.
